"Create a cozy, relaxing 2D platformer game with a calm and soothing atmosphere.

CORE GAMEPLAY:
- A cute character that can run, jump, and double-jump with smooth, forgiving, floaty controls
- No death or harsh penalties: if the player falls, they gently respawn at the last checkpoint
- Collect glowing items (stars, flowers, or fireflies) scattered across the levels
- 5 short levels, each with a gentle increase in challenge
- Simple moving platforms, bouncy mushrooms, and small puzzles (no enemies)

VISUAL STYLE:
- Soft pastel color palette with warm gradients (sunset, dawn, or twilight sky)
- Parallax background layers (hills, clouds, trees) with slow drifting motion
- Floating particles such as fireflies, falling petals, or soft snow
- Smooth, gentle animations (squash and stretch on jump, swaying grass)
- Rounded, minimalist, hand-drawn or low-poly look

AUDIO:
- Calming looping background music: soft piano, gentle guitar, or lo-fi ambient pads, slow tempo
- Ambient nature sounds (birds, wind, light rain, or flowing water)
- Soft, pleasant sound effects for jumping, landing, and collecting items
- Music fades smoothly between levels
- Volume sliders for music and sound effects, plus a mute button

UI:
- Minimal, clean HUD showing only the collected item count
- Start menu with the title and a \"Tap to Start\" button
- Pause menu and a calm \"Level Complete\" screen with a soft animation
- Hide all timers and scores that cause pressure

CONTROLS:
- Touch controls: left and right buttons on the left side, jump button on the right
- Also support keyboard (arrow keys/WASD + Space)

POLISH:
- Smooth performance (aim for 60 FPS)
- Auto-save progress

Start with a working core (movement, jumping, one level, background music), then add more levels, particles, and ambient sounds.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable cozy 2D platformer with relaxing visuals and audio, five levels, touch and keyboard controls, menus, and auto-save.

## Requirements
- Cute character with forgiving run, jump, and double-jump controls; gentle checkpoint respawns and no enemies.
- Five short levels with collectibles, moving platforms, bouncy mushrooms, and simple puzzles.
- Pastel scenery, parallax, particles, and smooth animations.
- Calming music and nature ambience, soft sound effects, level-to-level music fades, volume sliders, and mute.
- Minimal item-count HUD, start/pause/complete/settings screens, no timers or pressure-based scoring.
- Touch and keyboard controls; smooth performance and auto-save.
- Start with a working core, then add levels and polish.

## Decisions
- Built from scratch as a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game; audio is synthesized with Web Audio, avoiding external asset dependencies.
- Named the game **Lumen Hollow**; implemented five themed levels and progress persistence using local storage.
- Added a traversal test harness and adjusted level layouts and gate geometry based on automated playtesting.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game, five levels, movement and double-jump, collectibles, checkpoints, moving platforms, mushrooms, gates, goals, and gentle respawns.
- Parallax backgrounds, particles, character animation, themed level transitions, procedural music/ambience/effects, settings, and responsive touch controls.
- Start, pause, settings, completion UI, HUD, keyboard input, and auto-save.
- Automated browser checks and desktop/mobile screenshot review; level robot traversed all five levels after layout adjustments.

### Active
- Final verification after latest visual, audio, mobile, and gameplay polish changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run syntax checks and the browser playtest/visual capture scripts again after the latest edits.
2. Review the latest screenshots and resolve any remaining rendering or UI issues.
3. Check `git status` and report the resulting implementation and verification succinctly.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game shell and menu/HUD markup.
- `css/style.css`: Visual design, responsive layout, and UI styling.
- `js/main.js`: UI wiring, controls, settings, and auto-save.
- `js/game.js`: Canvas rendering, physics, level logic, and player visuals.
- `js/levels.js`: Five level layouts and themes.
- `js/background.js`: Parallax scenery and sky rendering.
- `js/audio.js`: Synthesized music, ambience, and sound effects.
- `js/fx.js`: Particle effects.
- `js/util.js`: Shared utilities.
- `screenshots/`: Browser captures from visual checks.

## Important Context
- Browser testing used a local server at `http://localhost:3002/`; temporary test scripts are under `/tmp/opencode/`, including `playtest.cjs` and `visuals.cjs`.
- Game test access is exposed as `window.__lumen`; the latest edits have not yet been rerun through the checks.
- No commit or push was reported.

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.

Built **Lumen Hollow**, a complete cozy platformer.

### What’s included
- Five themed levels with pastel parallax scenery, particles, flowers, fireflies, and animated water/weather.
- Forgiving movement with coyote time, buffered jumps, double jump, bouncy mushrooms, moving platforms, and gentle checkpoint respawns.
- Collectible firefly HUD, plus a final firefly-gated bloom puzzle.
- Start, pause, settings, and completion screens with auto-save and resume support.
- Keyboard controls and mobile touch controls.
- Synthesized generative music, ambience, and soft effects with volume sliders, mute, and level-to-level fades.
- Rendering caches for the parallax sky and vignette to improve performance on lower-end devices.

### Verification
- All five levels completed end-to-end in browser playtests.
- Confirmed double jump, mushroom bounce, moving-platform riding, checkpoint respawn, final gate unlock, and level progression.
- Verified star collection, settings, mute, auto-save, and progress restore after reload.
- Confirmed keyboard and touch input, responsive overlays, and zero console/runtime errors.
- Reviewed desktop and mobile screenshots.
